title: How to treat a UTI with AI and a real doctor
summary: Online UTI treatment and AI UTI treatment explained: first-line antibiotics, when you need a urine test, cash drug prices, and 7 telehealth services.
body_markdown:
Uncomplicated bladder infections in adult women can usually be evaluated from home by message, without waiting weeks for an office visit or making a two-hour clinic trip. Understanding how to treat a UTI with AI and a licensed physician starts with how the visit works: on FutureClinic, an AI assistant trained by your physician gathers your history first, and once you confirm the summary, a specific doctor with an MD, DO or MBBS degree reads your whole case, makes every medical decision, and sends your plan with a Human Signature (a live video or voice note). No form is approved in bulk.


Before choosing an online service, ask: did you want that service and its requirements, or a doctor of your own? If you want an antibiotic bundled into one checkout price or a reply in minutes, several services fit that need. If you wanted an expert doctor, FutureClinic gives you the same doctor over time, help with other problems in their specialty, and no subscription required. Messaging the same doctor over months lets you review a urine culture together, adjust a prescription that causes side effects, or look into why infections repeat. Every FutureClinic doctor you see works from one medical record.


## Can a bladder infection be treated by message?


A bladder infection (cystitis) is the most common urinary tract infection (UTI), occurring when bacteria multiply in the bladder ([NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/bladder-infection-uti-in-adults/definition-facts) ). About half of women get one in their lifetime, and about a quarter of them have repeat infections; the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) 2025 guideline sets lifetime UTI risk at 53% for women and 14% for men ([IDSA](https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/complicated-urinary-tract-infections/) ). Symptoms include burning when urinating, frequent or intense urges, lower belly pain, and cloudy, bloody or strong-smelling urine.


A 2002 *JAMA* review found that burning plus frequency without vaginal discharge or irritation raises UTI probability above 90%, ruling in the diagnosis from history alone. In a 2001 study of recurrent UTIs, 84% of 172 self-diagnosed episodes had a urinary pathogen on lab testing and 92% of confirmed episodes achieved cure. In a 2013 Pittsburgh study, physicians ordered urine cultures at 7% of online e-visits versus 31% of office visits, with identical three-week follow-up rates (7%) and 100% versus 92% guideline-recommended antibiotic prescribing. A 2023 study of 215,134 Minnesota UTI episodes found telemedicine used fewer lab tests with no increase in office visits, emergency visits or spending.


## First-line antibiotics for an uncomplicated UTI and cash prices


For women with uncomplicated bacterial cystitis, the American College of Physicians (ACP) 2021 guidance recommends one of three short-course oral antibiotics, if your doctor decides it's right for you (shorter than the 7-day Macrobid and 10-to-14-day Bactrim label courses) ([ACP](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33819054/) ):


-


**Nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals (Macrobid), 5 days (100 mg twice daily):** Trial side effects included nausea (8%), headache (6%) and gas (1.5%); it may turn urine brown, is not for kidney infection, and must not be used if creatinine clearance is under 60 mL/min. As of October 2026 on Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company, 10 capsules cost $6.38 before $5.25 shipping ($11.63 total) ([Cost Plus Drugs](https://api.costplusdrugs.com/pricelist/cpd) ).


-


**Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, or TMP-SMX (Bactrim DS), 3 days (800/160 mg twice daily):** Avoid with sulfa allergy; common side effects are stomach upset and skin rash (stop at the first sign of rash). As of October 2026 on Cost Plus Drugs, 6 tablets cost $5.23 before shipping ($10.48 total).


-


**Fosfomycin tromethamine (Monurol), single 3 g packet:** Dissolved in water; not for kidney infection or repeat doses; trial side effects included diarrhea (10.4%), headache (10.3%), vaginitis (7.6%) and nausea (5.2%). As of October 2026 on Cost Plus Drugs, one packet is $16.50 before shipping ($21.75 total).


Fluoroquinolones like ciprofloxacin carry a boxed warning for tendinitis, tendon rupture and neuropathy, and are reserved for patients with no alternative options. Newer FDA-approved pills include Pivya (2024), Orlynvah (2024) and Blujepa (2025). Finish your full course even if symptoms clear. Over-the-counter phenazopyridine relieves pain for up to two days, and cranberry products reduce repeat infections in some groups, but neither treats a UTI.


## Who needs a urine test or in-person care instead?


IDSA's July 2025 guideline defines an uncomplicated UTI as confined to the bladder without fever, chills or flank pain. Testing or in-person care is needed for:


-


**Fever, back or side pain, or nausea and vomiting:** Signs of kidney infection (pyelonephritis), a complicated UTI needing a urine culture and sometimes in-person or IV care.


-


**Men:** Acute prostatitis must be ruled out first; UK NICE guidance advises a urine culture before a 7-day antibiotic course.


-


**Pregnancy:** UTIs affect about 8% of pregnancies and increase preterm delivery risk. A urine culture is needed; nitrofurantoin is contraindicated at term (38 to 42 weeks) and TMP-SMX carries first-trimester risks.


-


**Repeat infections, catheters and children:** Repeat infections may call for imaging or other tests, and a UTI with a urinary catheter is generally not uncomplicated under IDSA 2025. Febrile children aged 2 to 24 months need urinalysis, culture and ultrasound.


A FutureClinic physician can order lab tests at discounted prices. FutureClinic is not for emergencies; call 911, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.
